1	# Transition-state symmetry and molecular graph representations
2	
3	This task uses ordinary transition-state theory (TST) and the graph
4	representation conventions of the Auto-Mech project.  The following context is
5	provided as a method reference, not as a solution for this particular source
6	snapshot.
7	
8	For a reaction rate in canonical TST, a common schematic form is
9	
10	\[
11	k(T) = \frac{k_B T}{h}\frac{Q^\ddagger(T)}{Q_R(T)}
12	       \exp\left[-\frac{\Delta E^\ddagger}{k_B T}\right],
13	\]
14	
15	where the molecular partition functions contain translational, rotational, and
16	vibrational contributions. The rotational contribution for a nonlinear
17	molecule contains a symmetry divisor \(\sigma\):
18	
19	\[
20	q_{\mathrm{rot}} \propto \frac{1}{\sigma}
21	  \sqrt{I_A I_B I_C}\,T^{3/2},
22	\]
23	
24	with the corresponding expression for a linear molecule using its nonzero
25	moments of inertia. The symmetry number is a property of the physical
26	molecular object and its indistinguishable rotations; equivalent presentations
27	of one object must not change the physical factor. See Truhlar, Garrett, and
28	Klippenstein, *Current Status of Transition-State Theory*,
29	<https://doi.org/10.1021/cr00016a001>.
30	
31	Auto-Mech stores molecular connectivity as a graph: atom keys map to tuples
32	containing an element symbol, implicit-hydrogen count, and stereo information;
33	bonds are keyed by unordered atom-key pairs and carry bond-order information.
34	Transition-state graphs use the same representation while allowing an
35	intermediate bond order between the reactant and product limits to encode a
36	forming or breaking connection. The supplied graph APIs expose connectivity,
37	reaction orientation, and rotor-coordinate observations. These are
38	data-structure contracts, not assumptions about a particular fixture.
39	
40	For this workbench, a valid graph has finite atom and bond maps, unordered bond
41	keys, chemically consistent implicit-hydrogen counts, and finite transition
42	edge orders. A physical rotor observation is represented by a sorted signature
43	of canonical element-symbol sequences along the public coordinate objects. A
44	coordinate and its reverse describe the same unoriented physical axis, so the
45	lexicographically smaller sequence is used. Each physically distinct,
46	nonredundant rotatable axis must be represented once; removing an axis merely
47	to make two presentations have the same count is not a valid repair. Equivalent
48	graph presentations must produce the same signature exactly (these are
49	discrete symbols, so no numerical tolerance is involved), while the supplied
50	changed-connectivity negative control must not be collapsed to the same
51	observation. Distinguish that physical invariant from an implementation
52	artifact.
53	
54	## References
55	
56	1. D. G. Truhlar, B. C. Garrett, and S. J. Klippenstein, “Current Status of
57	   Transition-State Theory,” *Chemical Reviews* 100 (2000), 2703–2796,
58	   <https://doi.org/10.1021/cr00016a001>.
59	2. Auto-Mech project documentation and source docstrings at the supplied
60	   source commit, <https://github.com/Auto-Mech/autochem>.
61	
62	The supplied source is the historical version under investigation.  The task

59	def kekule(gra, max_stereo_overlap=True):
60	    """One low-spin kekule graph, ignoring current bond orders
61	
62	    Low-spin kekule graphs have double and triple bonds assigned to
63	    minimize the number of unpaired electrons.
64	
65	    :param gra: molecular graph
66	    :type gra: automol graph data structure
67	    :param max_stereo_overlap: optionally, request as many stereo bonds as
68	        possible to have a bond order of 2
69	    :type max_stereo_overlap: bool
70	    :returns: a kekule graph
71	    """
72	    ste_bkeys = bond_stereo_keys(gra)
73	    nbkeys_dct = bonds_neighbor_bond_keys(gra, group=False)
74	
75	    def _count_stereo_double_bonds(gra):
76	        good_bkeys = good_stereo_bond_keys_from_kekule(
77	            gra, ste_bkeys=ste_bkeys, nbkeys_dct=nbkeys_dct
78	        )
79	        return len(good_bkeys)
80	
81	    def _count_ring_double_bonds(gra):
82	        len_rng = 0
83	        # extract rings and count alternate double bonds
84	        # maximize the total N of alternate double bonds in the molecule
85	        rngs_atm_keys = rings_atom_keys(gra)
86	        for rng_atm_keys in rngs_atm_keys:
87	            rng_bnd_keys = frozenset(map(frozenset, edges(rng_atm_keys)))
88	            good_bkeys = good_stereo_bond_keys_from_kekule(
89	                gra, ste_bkeys=rng_bnd_keys, nbkeys_dct=nbkeys_dct

91	            len_rng += len(good_bkeys)
92	        return len_rng

95	
96	    if not max_stereo_overlap:

## Root cause

The workflow observed different rotor axes for equivalent presentations of one TS: key-relableed presentations agreed, but `graph.ts.reverse(...)` yielded a different rotor `('C','C','C','H')` instead of `('H','C','S','H')`.

- A TS graph encodes forming bonds with order 0.1 and breaking bonds with 0.9; `ts.reverse` swaps these — same physical object, different presentation.
- In the rotor pipeline, neighbor selection used `ords_last=(0.1,)` — deprioritizing *forming* bonds but not *breaking* ones, so the chosen connections depended on reaction direction:
  - `linear_segment_cap_keys` (`_03kekule.py`): extending the linear segment `C–C` at atom 11 picked neighbor C-67 across the breaking bond in the forward direction, but H-41 once reversed — a different segment, a different rotational axis, and a swallowed rotor.
  - `rotational_coordinates` (`_06heur.py`): the out-of-line torsion reference at an axis end could flip similarly whenever a partial-bond neighbor competed with a full-bond neighbor.

## Repair (3 files, minimal and local to the rotor path)

- `source/automol/graph/base/_06heur.py`: in `rotational_segment_keys` and `rotational_coordinates`, pass `ords_last=()` so forming (0.1) and breaking (0.9) bonds are treated alike when identifying in-line neighbors and torsion references — the axis of a physical rotor cannot depend on reaction orientation. The forward-direction observation (one axis spanning `67–11–23–37`) is preserved for all presentations; no rotor is removed to force agreement.
- `source/automol/graph/base/_03kekule.py` and `source/automol/graph/base/_00core.py`: added an optional `ords_last` parameter (default `(0.1,)`, unchanged) to `linear_segment_cap_keys`, `linear_segments_atom_keys`, `atom(s)_zmat_sorted_neighbor_atom_keys`, and `atom_zmat_neighbor_atom_key` so every other consumer (SMILES, z-matrix construction, geometry conversion) keeps its exact prior behavior.
